run.change_description: fix(utils/body,validator): normalize Content-Type media type for case-insensitive matching

summary.intent: Make parseBody() and validator() match Content-Type media types case-insensitively (issue #5060) while leaving parameters such as multipart boundaries untouched.
summary.issue_fit: Partial: mixed-case JSON, urlencoded and multipart are now accepted with boundaries intact, but the switch to arrayBuffer() in parseBody's form path regresses parseBody after an earlier c.req.formData().
summary.coverage: Complete merge-base diff (6 files) read; HonoRequest body caching and the validator form path inspected. Reviewer-executed at the head: vitest on body, buffer and validator tests, 106 passed and 1 skipped; scratch esbuild probe comparing main and head, which reproduced the regression. Unused: Deno, Bun, Workers and Lambda runtime suites (unavailable offline); the Codecov and benchmark comments were not used. The change description and originating issue #5060 came from the caller-supplied packet, not a forge fetch.

findings.title: Reuse cached FormData in parseBody instead of re-serializing it
findings.trigger: A handler or middleware awaits `c.req.formData()` and then calls `c.req.parseBody()` on a multipart/form-data request.
findings.impact: parseBody now rejects with `TypeError: Failed to parse body as FormData.` because arrayBuffer() re-serializes the cached FormData with a new boundary that no longer matches the Content-Type header; the base returned the fields.
findings.change: In `parseFormData` in `src/utils/body.ts`, when the request is a HonoRequest with `bodyCache.formData` set, await and use that value. Otherwise read `arrayBuffer()`, call `bufferToFormData` and cache the result, as the form case in `src/validator/validator.ts` does.
